question: which committed results declare an input group built by a glob filtered on .exists(), so the declaration silently SHRINKS on a partial store instead of refusing
the_defect: ABSENCE IS SILENT. files_entry(name, [p for p in paths if p.exists()]) makes the declared group a function of the filesystem at write time rather than of the commit. On a partial store it neither refuses nor warns, and the result still reads as complete
interim: counts are measured; the classification of each varying group into legitimate scope or silent shrink is NOT done and is not claimed here

call_sites.why_the_brief_undercounted: 17 is what a one-line grep for files_entry.*exists() sees. The AST sees 18: scripts/trio_q100_phase.py:72 spans four lines with the filter on line 74

the_negative_the_lane_was_opened_on.reading: 312 in every one of the 13: NO SHRINK ANYWHERE. The defect is real as a mechanism and so far UNREALISED for this group. The 13-against-312 reported on 2026-10-10 was a worktree of this lane's own making, not any artefact

a_varying_count_is_not_itself_a_defect: a result that covered 23 chromosomes should declare 23. What a count cannot do is tell that from a result that meant 24 and silently got 23
does_not_claim: not that any committed result IS wrong; not that a varying member count is a defect (a result that covered fewer chromosomes should declare fewer); not that the constant-count groups are safe, since a group constant at a shrunken value would look identical to one constant at its full value; and nothing about groups built WITHOUT an exists() filter, which are the majority
the_limit_that_would_flatter_us: a group CONSTANT at a shrunken value is indistinguishable here from one constant at its full value, so the constant-count groups are NOT shown safe. test_PLANTED_a_group_constant_at_a_shrunken_value_is_INVISIBLE_here holds that as a test

sources.accession: the genomeos/ and scripts/ trees, read by AST

parameters.method: ast.parse over every .py, then every files_entry call; group declarations read from result_manifest.inputs where group is true
parameters.why_not_grep: a one-line pattern cannot see a call whose filter sits on a later line

exclusions: static only: nothing was run, no store was read, no result's bytes were touched, and no varying count is classified

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

partitions.none: one population, the committed registry; no partition is taken and the absence of one is not a claim of independence

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 3e43ef4

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
